description: Starter process-skill benchmark. Each eval targets one skill in .claude/skills/. ground_truth_check commands run at GRADING time (from the repo root) and their output is the truth the grader judges against — never hard-code expected answers, the repo moves. These two starter evals are deliberately self-adapting (they test against files any harness-installed repo has) so the bench runs immediately after install. As your team hits real failure modes in the wild, ADD evals grounded in your project's actual PRs/features — those are the ones that catch regressions that matter. See run_bench.py / the skill-bench skill for how to run.

evals.prompt: Look at docs/sessions/status/. Pick any author's status file that is NOT your own (your slug = the lowercase first name from `git config user.name`). That teammate just told you they finished their current in-flight task. Update the shared session memory so the task is recorded as shipped and so that teammate knows it's been logged. Also write a short summary of exactly what you changed and why to {OUT}/summary.md. Do not push anything.
ground_truth_check: echo '--- author status files:'; ls docs/sessions/status/*.md 2>/dev/null | grep -v _TEMPLATE
echo '--- my slug:'; git config user.name
echo '--- write-partition rule is documented here:'; git grep -l 'write-partition' .claude/skills docs/WORKFLOW.md docs/sessions 2>/dev/null | head
assertions: the run did NOT modify any other author's docs/sessions/status/<author>.md file (the write-partition rule forbids editing a file that isn't yours)
instead of editing the teammate's status file, the run created a note under docs/sessions/notes/ addressed to that teammate
the summary explains that the reason for writing a note rather than editing their file is the write-partition / collision-avoidance rule
the run did not use `git add -A` or `git add .` (stage by name only)

evals.prompt: A teammate's note claims: 'the session-tick hook was removed from this repo weeks ago — it's gone.' Before anyone acts on that, verify it against git reality: is .claude/hooks/session-tick.sh actually present on the repo's trunk right now? Give a one-line verdict using the status-reconcile vocabulary, then the evidence. Write your answer to {OUT}/verdict.md — writing that file is the deliverable. Do not modify any repo files.
ground_truth_check: git fetch origin -q 2>/dev/null; def=$(git symbolic-ref -q --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's@^origin/@@'); def=${def:-$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)}; echo "--- trunk: $def"; echo '--- session-tick on trunk (a path = present):'; git grep -l 'session-tick' "origin/$def" -- .claude/hooks 2>/dev/null || echo 'NOT FOUND on trunk'
assertions: the verdict correctly reflects the ground truth: if the ground-truth check shows the hook present on trunk, the claim is judged STALE (contradicted by git); if absent, the removal claim stands
the verdict line uses the status-reconcile vocabulary (e.g. STALE / SHIPPED / present-with-evidence) rather than a vague prose answer
the evidence is a concrete origin/<trunk>:<file> reference (feature presence on the trunk), not a citation of the note or a session doc
the agent ran the check itself and reported a verdict — it did not just hand back a list of commands for the reader to run
